## 4. Assumptions and limits

*Numbers carry markers and are verified by `check_prose.py`; tables are generated by `pp_limits.py`, `pp_strata.py`, `pp_wcurse.py` (see the Makefile).*

### 4.1 The same 168 groups, re-split
Every experiment of every branch draws from one labelled data set: 168 pair groups (521 judgments of which 51% are decisive, 14% ties and 35% "not applicable"), 284 distinct frames of 3 growth sessions (111, 108 and 65 frames). The comparison graph (frames as nodes, labelled groups as edges) falls into 117 connected components. A "new seed" changes the random split into initial / pool / validation / test groups, the random label draws and the training randomness; it never adds data. The held-out set of one seed has on average 63.5 (split A) or 53.2 (split B) decisive judgments. Consequences: (a) Wilcoxon p-values and bootstrap intervals over seeds describe the variability of splits, label draws and training, **not** sampling of new growth runs, so they are optimistic; (b) a pre-registered confirmation on unused seeds protects against selection on the development seeds, not against properties of these 168 groups; (c) per-type numbers, in particular HTR, rest on a handful of held-out judgments per seed and split.

### 4.2 Dense, near-duplicate frames
The frames are a nearly continuous sampling of three runs. Distances below are 1 − cosine similarity of the centred, normalised frozen SimCLR features (the geometry of the graph). The median distance of a held-out judgment's farther image to its nearest training image is 0.020 at budget 10 and 0.004 at budget 60; the nearer image is at 0.001 and 0.000 (median), and 97% of held-out judgments have an image within 0.01 of a training image at budget 60. For scale, the distance between two reference images of the same type has median 0.129, between different types 0.584. So test frames are not "new situations" but neighbours of training frames, which is exactly what a smoothness regulariser on a kNN graph can exploit. Strict de-duplication of the labelled data is not possible (red-team audit 2: at distance ≤ 0.002 only a minority of the candidate pool survives).

### 4.3 Anchor-near versus anchor-far judgments (secondary endpoint of every study)
The learners use typed ideal images ("anchors"); many of them are near-copies of trajectory frames. Of the 2359 held-out judgments of the red-team development block, 47% involve an image within 0.001 of some typed anchor (39% for the reference images alone), 22% have both images farther than 0.03 from every anchor ("anchor-far"; 29% for references alone). The **anchor-far secondary endpoint** is the AUC / accuracy computed on these judgments only. Table (AUC gain by stratum; development block, 20 seeds, red-team per-judgment predictions; split A / split B; the last two rows use budgets 20 and 40 only):

{{INCLUDE:tables/strata_summary.md}}

Reading, honestly (red-team **confirmation block**, 35 unused seeds; the development block, 20 seeds, is in the table as well): (i) the gain of the best learner over the tuned graph-free control is clearly positive in anchor-near judgments (+0.035 / +0.037 AUC), about zero in the bands between (0.001 to 0.01: +0.001 / −0.000; 0.01 to 0.03: −0.002 / −0.002) and positive again in anchor-far judgments (>0.03: +0.019 / +0.013 AUC with intervals above or touching zero, accuracy +0.029 / +0.029). With the red team's own threshold 0.01 the far stratum mixes the empty middle band into it and the AUC gain is +0.003 / +0.001: **the anchor-far verdict depends on the threshold**, and only about 12 judgments per (seed, budget, draw) cell lie beyond 0.03, so this stratum is noisy; the red team's frozen RT1 rule (threshold 0.01, one Holm family with its de-duplication and time-blocked tests) is its to report; (ii) by component: the Laplacian regulariser's gain over aw8_all stays positive anchor-far (>0.03: +0.013 / +0.027; >0.01: +0.009 / +0.010), whereas the extra gain of the four-fold schedule over lap3_k10 sits in anchor-near judgments (+0.021 / +0.018) and is not resolved anchor-far (+0.012 / −0.001 at >0.03; −0.003 / −0.006 at >0.01); (iii) the earlier anchor-weight gain (aw8_all over the default head) is as large in anchor-far judgments (+0.020 / +0.034) as anywhere, so it is not an anchor-copy artefact; (iv) a time-blocked evaluation (whole 100-frame blocks of a run held out, 25-frame buffer removed from training groups, candidate pool and graph; red-team audit 3, development block) keeps the gain: AUC +0.026 [+0.021, +0.031], accuracy +0.012 [+0.004, +0.020] over the tuned graph-free control, and +0.114 AUC over the shuffled-graph control (table `tables/redteam_extra.md`); this split still stays inside the three known runs. The strata of the red-team confirmation block are added to `tables/strata.csv` automatically once all of its per-judgment files exist (they did when this package was built).
**Only the red team's learners have an anchor-far version**: the confirmation cells of the individual studies store aggregated metrics only, so the claims of the other branches (GM, GE, selection) have no anchor-far check; re-running them with per-judgment output is listed in `GPU_TASKS_paper_package.md`.

### 4.4 Tuned on development seeds (winner's curse)
Every frozen candidate was chosen on development seeds that share the 168 groups with the confirmation seeds: the anchor weight 8, lambda 3 with k 10, the factor 4 and the graph-free control's schedule (steps ×2, learning rate ×0.5; chosen on 12 to 20 development seeds). The table compares the development gain with the gain on the pre-registered confirmation seeds for the same learner pair (ratio = confirmation / development; 40 cells; median 0.93, range 0.50 to 2.42, 65% of the cells below 1):

{{INCLUDE:tables/winners_curse.md}}

The confirmation, not the development number, is the evidence; the typical shrinkage is small but single cells lose up to half of the development effect. The "tuned graph-free control" is tuned on one dimension only (steps and learning rate); other graph-free regularisers were tried only in development (consistency regularisation comes within −0.005 / −0.007 AUC of the best learner).

### 4.5 Other limits
- **Endpoint.** All learner and selection claims are about held-out preference judgments. On the paper's own endpoint (type accuracy of 28 ideal images) no learner or graph method beats 1-NN in a way attributable to the learner (claim G6); that endpoint cannot rank methods.
- **Controls are weak or narrow.** A shuffled graph is far worse than no graph (claim G3), so beating it is a low bar; the noisy-graph and non-graph controls are more informative but exist only for part of the claims.
- **Harsh splits.** The held-out-run and held-out-temperature tests use fixed test sets (50 and 26 judgments); the second confirmation block reuses the same test judgments, and test-group bootstrap intervals include zero in 7 of 8 cases.
- **Frozen features, CPU only.** Nothing was tested with an end-to-end fine-tuned encoder; the learner results are for a head on cached SimCLR features.
- **Selection** was examined single-shot from the initial model; sequential rounds with the best learner and selection from a cold start under `lap3_k10_st4` were not examined.
- **Branches not in the package yet.** Studies of other conversations that had no result files when this package was built (representation, anchor exchange, temporal graph) and the red team's confirmation block are not included; see the README for how to add them.
